messages:
marc: heads up — we just received a user erase/subject request and the automatic delete job failed. looks like the service account that runs the eraser was removed in last week's authz cleanup.
lucy: ugh. error logs?
marc: paste from job log:

ERROR: erase-runner: attempt=1 user_id=U-98127 status=FAILED
reason=KMS.DecryptFailed
trace=AccessDeniedException: serviceAccount:service-eraser@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com does not have permission to decrypt key projects/redwood-kms/locations/global/keyRings/vec-keys/cryptoKeys/emb-ck/cryptoKeyVersions/3

marc: also saw this in snapshot cleanup step:

2025-09-03T12:14:07Z fetch-snapshot: snapshot=proj-U-98127-20250901-embed.gcs bucket-read ok
2025-09-03T12:14:08Z decrypt-layer: failed to open envelope: AccessDenied

henry: that aligns with my memory — we merged an RBAC PR (PR #3421) to remove the old eraser service account from the project last Friday. thought the new runner would use the ephemeral svcacct but the rollout didn't finish.
marc: right. rough flow: delete job calls vectorstore->snapshot downloader -> KMS decrypt -> delete vectors + mark tombstone. decrypt failing means we can't verify deletes for some material.
elaine: legal: we need an evidence chain for the user's request. if we cannot decrypt snapshots immediately, preserve everything in place and document timeline. we cannot claim deletion until it's verifiable. also need a signed attestation if we do a breakglass.
privacy-bot: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/privacy/erase-failures — steps 1-6. recommended: do NOT delete snapshots until a temporary audit key is used or svcacct is restored. include ticket id in logs.
marc: proposed remediation options:
  1) re-grant decrypt IAM to service-eraser for the specific key and run purge, then revoke — fastest.
  2) if key rotation blocked that, request KMS rewrap to a key the eraser can access (requires ops approval + legal attestation).
  3) if neither, restore a snapshot to a staging project where an oncall with breakglass can run a manual erase (forensics present).

which is safest/legal?
elaine: preference 1 if we can do least-privilege grant scoped to single key and timebox it. require a signed approval from Privacy + Legal + Ops before regrant. capture all IAM changes in the audit log and snapshot the key version metadata.
henry: ops-oncall — can you check if the service-eraser account still exists in IAM history and whether the key binding was removed or if the key itself rotated to a new version?
ops-oncall: looking. initial read: svcacct was disabled by org:authz-bot during cleanup at 2025-09-01T03:02:11Z. KMS key has version 3 active; version 2 had previous bindings. I can re-enable the svcacct for a 30m window if legal signs off.
marc: sample commands I ran locally (for context):

# check IAM binding
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy emb-ck --location global --keyring vec-keys --project redwood-kms

# attempted decrypt (failed)
echo "ciphertext" | gcloud kms decrypt --location global --keyring vec-keys --key emb-ck --ciphertext-file - --plaintext-file -

# job snapshot listing
gsutil ls gs://embeddings-snapshots/proj-U-98127*/

lucy: if we do temporary regrant, also add an audit hook that snapshots all API responses from the eraser (or log everything to sealed bucket). need immutable evidence for legal.
elaine: yes. add immutable evidence bundle (seal to legal-bucket with retention and strict ACL). record cross-check: job run id, user id, key version, who approved.
marc: ok I'll open SR-2026-9876 and tag ops/legal/privacy. action items:
  - marc: open ticket + attach logs + link runbook (doing now).
  - ops-oncall: standby to enable svcacct for 30m once legal confirms. add Cloud Audit log export of IAM change.
  - henry/lucy: add a short script to re-run deletes idempotently and emit verification hashes for the user record.
  - elaine: confirm breakglass approval format and who signs.

ops-oncall: noted. I can do quick enable but will wait for the signed doc. will also create a temporary audit snapshot and export IAM diff.
privacy-bot: checklist added to ticket SR-2026-9876. link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/SR-2026-9876
marc: if we choose not to regrant, we need a retention-exception request ASAP (include forensic reasons) so we don't breach SLA for the user. legal: what is the max window?
elaine: retention exception can be requested but approvals vary. for now we must preserve data integrity and stop any automated purges. don't respond to the requester claiming completed until we have verifiable deletion. I'll draft a short approval template.
henry: follow-up: we'll add a guard in the pipeline — if KMS decrypt fails, mark job as FAILED_HOLD and notify privacy-team rather than retrying. small code change but prevents accidental false-successes.
lucy: I can PR a health-check for the svcacct mapping and a preflight that ensures the eraser can decrypt at least one test envelope before starting.
marc: thanks all. i'll collect approvals and update SR-2026-9876 when we have a path. reaction: :eyes: :lock: :thumbsup:
